title: Getting research into health policy decisions
summary: A research team has studied ways to raise childhood vaccination rates. The project aims to get the findings used by the national health ministry and district health offices when they plan the next immunisation programme.
whyThisWorks: Research projects often stop at publishing. This example treats use of the evidence as the goal. Activities start before the study, by agreeing questions with the people who will use the answers. Outcomes follow three kinds of research impact: understanding (conceptual), skills (capacity building), then changes in plans and budgets (instrumental). Assumptions name the political risks, such as timing and changes of government. It also reflects a shift under way: officials increasingly reach evidence through AI tools, often with smaller teams. So the project publishes findings in forms those tools can read accurately, and trains analysts to check AI summaries. There is little evidence yet on how AI changes research uptake, so treat this part as a hypothesis to test.

items: District health officials plan vaccination campaigns with little local evidence. Studies arrive as long reports, after decisions are made.
assumptions: Officials use evidence when it arrives on time and in a usable form

indicators.text: Share of district immunisation plans citing research evidence
indicators.target: Tracked for context. Targets are set at outcome level.

items: Agree research questions with ministry staff before the study starts
Share findings in two-page briefs timed to the budget cycle
Run 45-minute evidence sessions for district health officials
Publish data and plain summaries that AI tools can find and cite
Train 30 ministry analysts to judge evidence, including AI summaries
Present results at the national immunisation planning meeting
assumptions: Ministry staff have time to take part
Study results are ready before planning starts

indicators.text: Number of evidence sessions held with district officials

items: Research questions agreed with the ministry in writing
Four policy briefs published before budget deadlines
Evidence sessions reach officials from 20 districts
Open data and a plain summary online for every finding
30 analysts trained to judge evidence and AI summaries
assumptions: Briefs reach the people who draft the plans
AI tools used by ministry staff represent the findings accurately
Trained officials stay in post long enough to use it

indicators.text: Districts with at least one official at an evidence session
indicators.target: 20 of 25 districts by the end of year 1

items: Officials understand what the study found and how strong it is
Analysts check evidence and AI summaries when advising on plans
Ministry staff ask the team for evidence on new questions
assumptions: The findings fit the ministry's priorities and budget

indicators.text: Trained analysts passing an evidence-use assessment

items: More district plans use the study's findings
The ministry budgets for the approach in its next plan
assumptions: A change of government doesn't reverse priorities
Funding exists to scale the approach up

indicators.text: District immunisation plans that cite the study's findings

items: More children are fully vaccinated on time across the country
assumptions: Vaccine supply and health workers keep pace with demand

indicators.text: Share of children fully vaccinated by age 2

draftPairs.improved: Evidence sessions reach officials from 20 districts
draftPairs.why: 'Informed' can't be counted, and it hides whether anyone actually came. The improved version names who was reached and how many.

draftPairs.improved: More district plans use the study's findings
draftPairs.why: Policy change has many causes, and few studies can claim it alone. A specific, visible use of the findings is something the team can track and credibly contribute to.
